In this regard, we do have reservations about the assumption that past estimates of flood plain extent will continue to be accurate in the future: due to the increased urbanization of large portions of drainage basins, it is likely that the probabilities of flooding given portions of the flood plains have also increased. The final statements should therefore identify and evaluate the flood plain estimates and provide this information on topographic maps comparable to those of the USGS.
The reasoning expressed in the several statements (e.g., pages 63 - 64, Milton-Turbot) on the dangers of flood plain development is very well taken. A dilemma arises when strong public support exists simultaneously for both a restoration of pre-flood living patterns and protection from future disaster. Flood plain management is effected through both the Urban Renewal plans and the local flood control ordinances. We think it would be useful to identify the extent of flooding with respect to various probabilities (e.g., 10, 50, 100, record-year floods) and to propose land uses and structural requirements compatible with each. Thus, the flood plain would not be treated as a homogeneous area of equal danger, with uniform protective measures.
Of similar importance is the need for effective flood plain management upstream and downstream from the present study areas: actions taken at one point along a river directly affect flood heads and flow velocities at other places. While such action is beyond the scope of any one of the various renewal projects, your office should consider a cooperative effort with the counties and municipalities which share the locational problems of disaster preparedness.
Our comments above notwithstanding, the renewal plans, if implemented, represent a reasonable balance between the two conflicting planning goals of restoration and protection. We also would agree with the statements' conclusions that long-term environmental degradation of the air, water, and noise environs will not result from the proposed actions. It is our hope that the people in the flooded areas will appreciate the importance of effective flood plain controls and the necessary changes in living patterns which must occur if the effects of future disasters are to be minimized.
